summary: Frontend-only verification of PublicChrome header/footer on /auctions and /auctions/doesnotexist/live. All requested checks passed: header brand + 6 nav links (Auctions marked is-on), Sign in/Register testids, dark footer (rgb(15,42,34)) with Open notices/Auctions/Help Centre/Trust & security/Privacy + '© 2026 PMC Managers Limited'. All 14 header/footer link navigations from /auctions went to the correct routes. Empty state 'No live auctions right now' shown with 0 auction cards. Invalid room renders public-auction-spectator-error (data-pmc-e-page=public-chrome) with spectator-error 'Auction unavailable / Auction not found' INSIDE the chrome; room Sign in -> /login and footer Privacy -> /privacy work. No pageerrors, no blank page. Mobile 390px: no horizontal overflow; global mobile topbar takes over as on other public pages.

issues: Body wrapper is 'min-h-screen' inside PublicChrome, so content area = 100vh plus the 73px header; the footer always sits below the fold with a big empty beige gap even when the page has only an empty-state card. Consider min-height: calc(100vh - header) or flex column layout.
Header 'EN' language button has no onClick and no data-testid (decorative; same as other public pages presumably).

action_items: Optional: reduce min-h-screen inside PublicChrome children so footer is not pushed far below short content.
Optional: add data-testid to PublicChrome nav links/footer links/brand for easier automation (currently only signin/register have testids).
critical_code_review_comments: PublicChrome nav/footer links lack data-testid attributes (only public-chrome-signin/register).
PublicChrome relies on the global PmcIconSprite for #i-globe (present, verified).
context_for_next_testing_agent: PublicChrome verified on /auctions (testid public-auctions-page) and invalid room (public-auction-spectator-error). Selectors used: header.pmc-chrome .pmc-nav a, footer.pmc-chrome a, [data-testid=public-chrome-signin|register]. No auction data seeded; live-room happy path chrome (public-auction-spectator) not exercised visually.
